chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Hamdan al-Qalanisi, from Muhammad ibn al-Walid, from Aban, from Aamir ibn Abdullah ibn Juza'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no one who recites the end of Surah Al-Kahf before sleeping except that he will wake up at the time he desires.

key_terms.آخِرَ الْكَهْفِ: The end of Surah Al-Kahf (Chapter 18 of the Quran)
key_terms.تَيَقَّظَ: He will wake up / become alert
key_terms.عِنْدَ النَّوْمِ: Before sleeping / at the time of sleep

ai.seo_question: What is the benefit of reciting the end of Surah Al-Kahf before sleeping?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), establishing a specific spiritual practice (‘adah) where reciting the final verses of Surah Al-Kahf serves as a means of divine assistance (tawfiq) for conscious awakening. This highlights the Shia understanding of Quranic verses as possessing inherent barakah that can influence physical states, linking the protection from the Dajjal mentioned in the chapter’s context to the regulation of sleep cycles.
